Control Statement: The information security policy set is approved by the CISO, published to all personnel and relevant vendors, and reviewed and updated at least once every 12 months. Roles and responsibilities are defined in the policy.
Evidence: Policy library export showing version, approval date, and approver; intranet publication page; annual review ticket
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Executive management assigns accountability for protecting cardholder data and for the PCI DSS compliance program through a written charter. Information security responsibility is formally assigned to the CISO.
Evidence: Signed PCI program charter; board or executive committee minutes showing communication of the charter
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: An enterprise risk assessment is performed annually and on significant change. It identifies threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood, impact, fraud risk, and changes in the business, and is approved by the Risk Committee.
Evidence: Risk register export with ratings and owners; Risk Committee approval minutes
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: A targeted risk analysis (TRA) is documented for each PCI DSS requirement that lets the entity set its own frequency (for example 7.2.5.1, 10.4.2.1, 11.3.1.1, 12.10.4.1, and 11.6.1 if not weekly). Each TRA is reviewed at least once every 12 months.
Evidence: TRA documents with assets, threats, likelihood and impact factors, justification, reviewer and date
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: PCI DSS scope is documented and confirmed at least once every six months and on significant change: data flows, account data storage locations, in-scope inventory, segmentation controls, and third-party connections. Organizational changes trigger a documented scope impact review.
Evidence: Signed scope confirmation memo (two per year); updated data-flow diagram; in-scope inventory export; change tickets flagged as significant
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: At least once every three months the PCI program owner confirms that personnel are performing daily log reviews, NSC configuration reviews, application of configuration standards to new systems, alert response, and change management. Each review is documented.
Evidence: Quarterly operational review workpaper with samples inspected, results, and sign-off
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Control deficiencies from internal testing, external audits, assessments, and pen tests are logged in the GRC platform with owner, risk rating, and due date, tracked to closure, and reported monthly to the Risk Committee. Items inside the GovRAMP boundary are also tracked on the POA&M.
Evidence: GRC platform issue register export; monthly Risk Committee deck; POA&M
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: The GovRAMP continuous monitoring package is prepared and submitted monthly: POA&M, updated inventory workbook, OS, database, and web application vulnerability scans, compliance scan results, risk adjustments, operational requirements, false positives, and an executive summary.
Evidence: Monthly submission confirmation from the GovRAMP document repository; the package files; PMO review result
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Access to in-scope systems is requested in ServiceNow and approved by the user's manager and the system owner before provisioning. Birthright access is granted through SCIM-enabled Okta groups. Non-birthright access follows the approval workflow. Access is mapped to job function and least privilege.
Evidence: ServiceNow access request with approvals and timestamps; Okta System Log group membership events
Test Procedure Ref: TP-01 (03-itgc-test-procedures/01-user-provisioning.md)

Control Statement: Employee terminations entered in the HRIS trigger automated Okta deactivation on the termination date with SCIM deprovisioning to downstream apps (ServiceNow, GitHub, GRC platform, Splunk). Contractor terminations are submitted by the sponsoring manager through a ServiceNow offboarding task. Accounts outside Okta (legacy batch system local accounts, database local accounts) are removed manually by the system owner the same business day.
Evidence: HRIS termination report; contractor roster with end dates; Okta System Log user.lifecycle.deactivate events; ServiceNow offboarding tasks
Test Procedure Ref: TP-02 (03-itgc-test-procedures/02-termination-deprovisioning.md)

Control Statement: Okta and the legacy batch system automatically disable user accounts after 90 days of inactivity.
Evidence: Okta inactivity automation configuration; legacy system security settings screenshot with parameters visible; list of accounts disabled by the rule
Test Procedure Ref: TP-AUTO (test of one plus ITGC reliance; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Privileged and CDE access is reviewed quarterly and all other user access to in-scope systems at least every six months. Reviewers certify each account, inappropriate access is removed and tracked to completion, and management acknowledges the results.
Evidence: Review campaign export with reviewer decisions and timestamps; source listings with query parameters; removal tickets; management sign-off
Test Procedure Ref: TP-03 (03-itgc-test-procedures/03-periodic-and-privileged-access-review.md)

Control Statement: Human administrative access to AWS is only through Okta SSO into IAM Identity Center permission sets. No IAM users exist for people; two vaulted break-glass IAM users are the documented exception. Root credentials are vaulted with hardware MFA and any root use alerts the SOC. Privileged roles are limited to approved members.
Evidence: IAM credential report; Identity Center permission set assignments; root-login alert rule and test alert
Test Procedure Ref: TP-AUTO (test of one plus ITGC reliance; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2) is enforced by Okta for all workforce sign-ins, including all non-console access into the CDE and all remote access. MFA cannot be bypassed except through a documented, time-limited exception approved by the CISO.
Evidence: Okta authentication policy configuration; Okta System Log showing per-session MFA challenge (not enrollment status); exception register
Test Procedure Ref: TP-AUTO (test of one plus ITGC reliance; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Where passwords are used, systems enforce at least 12 characters with letters and numbers, lock the account after no more than 10 failed attempts for at least 30 minutes, and require re-authentication after 15 minutes idle.
Evidence: Okta password and session policy settings; legacy system and database parameter exports with system name and date visible
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Application and system accounts are inventoried, assigned least privilege, blocked from interactive login where possible, and have credentials stored in AWS Secrets Manager (never hard coded) with rotation. Their access is reviewed every six months per the TRA.
Evidence: Service account inventory; Secrets Manager rotation configuration; secrets scanning results; semiannual review sign-off
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Direct query access to databases holding stored cardholder data is limited to the DBA role. All other users and applications reach the data through programmatic methods with least privilege.
Evidence: Database role and grant listings; list of DBA role members tied to approvals
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Third-party remote access accounts (for example colocation hardware vendor support) are disabled by default, enabled only for an approved ticket and time window, monitored while in use, and disabled afterward.
Evidence: Vendor access tickets with approval and window; account enable and disable events; session logs
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Role changes recorded in the HRIS create a ServiceNow task for the old manager and system owners to remove access no longer needed within five business days. SCIM removes old birthright groups automatically.
Evidence: HRIS job change report; ServiceNow transfer tasks with completion dates; Okta group removal events
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: All in-scope workforce applications authenticate through Okta SSO (SAML 2.0 or OIDC). Where the application supports SCIM, accounts and group membership are provisioned and deprovisioned from Okta. Apps without SSO or SCIM are listed as exceptions and their local accounts are included in ACC-04 reviews.
Evidence: Okta application inventory showing SSO protocol and SCIM status; exception list; sample SCIM provisioning and deprovisioning events
Test Procedure Ref: TP-AUTO (test of one plus ITGC reliance; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Privileged access to production AWS accounts and root/sudo on the legacy batch system is granted just in time through the PAM workflow: request tied to an approved ServiceNow ticket, time-bound elevation that expires automatically (4 hours default, 8 maximum), and session logging. No standing production write access exists for people.
Evidence: PAM or Identity Center elevation log with ticket IDs, start and expiry times; configuration showing maximum duration; list of standing privileged assignments (expected none beyond break-glass)
Test Procedure Ref: TP-AUTO for expiry configuration plus a sample of 25 elevations for ticket approval

Control Statement: IAM Access Analyzer (organization unused access analyzer, 90-day window) and external access findings are reviewed monthly. Unused roles, keys, and permissions are removed or justified. Removals go through Terraform and CHG-01.
Evidence: Monthly Access Analyzer findings export with disposition; linked change records; reviewer sign-off
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Production changes to applications and infrastructure (Terraform) require a ServiceNow change record with risk rating, test evidence, and approval by the change advisory board or a pre-approved standard change model before deployment. Emergency changes get retrospective approval within two business days.
Evidence: ServiceNow change records linked to GitHub pull requests and deployment logs; emergency change report
Test Procedure Ref: TP-04 (03-itgc-test-procedures/04-change-management.md)

Control Statement: GitHub branch protection on production repositories requires at least one approving review from someone other than the author and passing status checks before merge. The rule is enforced for administrators.
Evidence: Branch protection settings export (API) per repository; audit log of settings changes; sample merged pull requests
Test Procedure Ref: TP-04 (03-itgc-test-procedures/04-change-management.md)

Control Statement: The CI pipeline runs static analysis, dependency (software composition) scanning, and secrets scanning on every pull request. High and critical findings block merge. An inventory of bespoke software and third-party components (SBOM) is kept. Developers complete secure coding training every 12 months.
Evidence: Pipeline configuration; scan results attached to pull requests; SBOM export; training completion report
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Pre-production runs in separate AWS accounts with separate access. Live PANs are not used outside production. Test data and test accounts are removed before a system goes live.
Evidence: AWS Organizations account structure; SCPs; PAN discovery results for non-production; go-live checklist
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Only the CI/CD deployment role (GitHub Actions through OIDC) can change production. Developers have read-only production access. Emergency write access uses just-in-time elevation tied to a ticket and expires automatically.
Evidence: IAM role trust policies; permission set listings; CloudTrail events showing deployer identity; elevation log
Test Procedure Ref: TP-04 (03-itgc-test-procedures/04-change-management.md)

Control Statement: When a change is flagged as significant, the team confirms that applicable PCI DSS requirements are in place on new or changed systems (logging, anti-malware, configuration standard, scans, segmentation) and updates documentation before closing the change.
Evidence: Significant change checklist attached to the change record; post-change scan results
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: All scripts on the hosted payment page are inventoried with a written justification, authorized before release, and integrity-protected with Content Security Policy and Subresource Integrity.
Evidence: Script inventory with justification and approver; CSP header; SRI hashes in page source; change records for script additions
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: A change- and tamper-detection service evaluates the HTTP security headers and script contents of the hosted payment page as received by a browser at least weekly (configured to run every few hours) and alerts the SOC on unauthorized change.
Evidence: Tool configuration showing pages and frequency; run history; sample alert and ticket
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Systems are built from hardened, CIS-based images. Vendor default accounts are removed or changed. AWS Config conformance packs and AWS Security Hub (AWS Foundational Security Best Practices and PCI DSS v4.0.1 standards) detect drift from the configuration standard and alert the platform team.
Evidence: Configuration standard document; image build pipeline; AWS Config compliance history; Security Hub enabled with standards
Test Procedure Ref: TP-AUTO (test of one plus ITGC reliance; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: AWS Backup plans take daily backups of production RDS and critical EBS volumes with 35-day retention, cross-region copy, and vault lock. The legacy batch database is backed up nightly to encrypted storage. Backup failures open a ServiceNow incident.
Evidence: AWS Backup plan configuration; Backup Audit Manager report; job history; failure incidents
Test Procedure Ref: TP-05 (03-itgc-test-procedures/05-backup-and-restore.md)

Control Statement: Restores of the payment database and the legacy batch database are tested quarterly. Data integrity is checked and results are documented and reviewed.
Evidence: Restore test record with timestamps, row-count and checksum comparison, and reviewer sign-off
Test Procedure Ref: TP-05 (03-itgc-test-procedures/05-backup-and-restore.md)

Control Statement: Nightly settlement, remittance, and ACH file jobs are scheduled and monitored. Failures and control-total mismatches create ServiceNow incidents that are resolved, and reruns are approved and documented.
Evidence: Scheduler job history; control-total reconciliation reports; incident tickets with resolution
Test Procedure Ref: TP-06 (03-itgc-test-procedures/06-batch-job-monitoring.md)

Control Statement: CloudWatch alarms track capacity (CPU, database connections, queue depth). Auto scaling is configured for the payment tier. Capacity is reviewed monthly and before seasonal peaks such as license renewal periods.
Evidence: Alarm configuration; monthly capacity review record; auto scaling policy
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: The in-scope system component inventory is generated from AWS Config and the CMDB, includes function and use, and is reconciled monthly. The same inventory feeds the GovRAMP inventory workbook.
Evidence: Inventory export with reconciliation notes; GovRAMP inventory workbook
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: EDR anti-malware runs on all EC2 instances, colocation servers, and workstations with automatic updates and real-time or behavioral scanning. Systems judged not at risk for malware are re-evaluated periodically.
Evidence: EDR console coverage report reconciled to inventory; policy settings; evaluation record for excluded systems
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Audit logging is enabled for all in-scope components: an organization CloudTrail trail in all regions with log file validation, VPC flow logs, OS, application, database, and Okta logs. Logs capture the required events and details and are forwarded to the SIEM.
Evidence: CloudTrail trail configuration; SIEM source coverage report reconciled to inventory; sample log records
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Logs are written to a dedicated log-archive account in S3 with Object Lock and restricted read access, and retained for 12 months with three months immediately searchable in the SIEM. Log integrity is monitored.
Evidence: S3 Object Lock and bucket policy; SIEM retention settings; access listing for the log account
Test Procedure Ref: TP-AUTO (test of one plus ITGC reliance; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: SIEM correlation rules review security events and logs from CDE, critical, and security components daily. Alerts are triaged by the SOC, and exceptions are investigated and resolved. Other components are reviewed at the frequency set in the TRA.
Evidence: Rule inventory; alert queue export with triage timestamps; sampled alert tickets
Test Procedure Ref: TP-07 (03-itgc-test-procedures/07-logging-and-alert-response.md)

Control Statement: Failures of critical security control systems (network security controls, IDS/IPS, change detection, anti-malware, physical and logical access controls, audit logging, segmentation, audit log review, automated security testing) generate alerts. Failures are responded to promptly, with cause, duration, and remediation documented.
Evidence: Heartbeat and log-source-silence alert rules; failure tickets with root cause and duration
Test Procedure Ref: TP-07 (03-itgc-test-procedures/07-logging-and-alert-response.md)

Control Statement: All systems synchronize time to Amazon Time Sync Service or the designated internal time source. Time settings can only be changed by administrators.
Evidence: Chrony or NTP configuration from the image baseline; configuration compliance result
Test Procedure Ref: TP-AUTO (test of one plus ITGC reliance; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Amazon GuardDuty and network intrusion detection at the CDE and colocation boundaries alert on intrusions and on covert malware communication channels such as DNS tunneling.
Evidence: GuardDuty enabled in all accounts and regions; IDS placement diagram; sample alerts
Test Procedure Ref: TP-AUTO (test of one plus ITGC reliance; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: File integrity monitoring watches critical system files, configuration files, and payment page source files, compares them at least weekly, and alerts on unauthorized change.
Evidence: FIM policy with monitored paths; scan schedule; sample alert with investigation
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Authenticated internal vulnerability scans of all in-scope components run monthly and after significant change. High and critical findings are fixed and confirmed by rescan. Systems that cannot accept credentials are documented. Lower-risk findings follow the TRA timelines.
Evidence: Scanner job configuration showing credentials used; monthly reports; rescan evidence; list of credential-exempt systems
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: A PCI SSC Approved Scanning Vendor runs external scans at least once every three months and after significant change. Rescans are run until a passing result is achieved.
Evidence: ASV scan reports and attestations of scan compliance for four quarters; rescan reports
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Vulnerabilities are ranked using CVSS, exploitability, and known-exploited status. Keystone's patch SLA is 15 days for critical, 30 days for high, 90 days for moderate, and 180 days for low. That meets PCI DSS 6.3.3 (critical within one month) and GovRAMP ConMon timelines (high 30, moderate 90, low 180 days).
Evidence: Vulnerability management policy; patch compliance report; SLA aging report; POA&M entries for late items
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Internal and external penetration tests, including application-layer testing of the hosted payment page and APIs, are performed at least every 12 months and after significant change by a qualified, organizationally independent tester using the documented methodology. Exploitable findings are corrected and retested.
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 (GovRAMP Moderate b: CA-8; CA-8(1) [not in NIST 800-53B Moderate; see 02 notes]
Evidence: Pen test methodology; rules of engagement; tester qualifications; report; retest letter
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Segmentation controls (AWS account and VPC boundaries, security groups, Transit Gateway route tables, colocation firewall) are penetration tested at least every six months and after any change to segmentation, covering all segmentation methods in use.
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 (GovRAMP Moderate b: CA-8 [not in NIST 800-53B Moderate; see 02 notes]; SC-7
Evidence: Segmentation test reports (two per year); list of segmentation controls tested reconciled to scope documentation
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: AWS WAF with managed and custom rules protects the hosted payment page and agency APIs in blocking mode. WAF logs go to the SIEM.
Evidence: WAF web ACL configuration showing blocking mode; association with CloudFront and ALB; SIEM WAF log source
Test Procedure Ref: TP-AUTO (test of one plus ITGC reliance; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Hardware and software technologies in use are reviewed at least every 12 months for vendor support and end-of-life. A senior management approved plan exists to remediate outdated technology.
Evidence: Technology review record; end-of-life roadmap approved by management
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Network security controls (security groups, NACLs, Transit Gateway routes, colocation firewall) are defined in Terraform or managed configuration, follow a documented standard, and change only through CHG-01. Allowed services, protocols, and ports have a documented business need.
Evidence: NSC standard; Terraform repository history; ports and protocols register with justifications
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Network security control rule sets are reviewed at least once every six months to confirm each rule is still needed and effective. Stale rules are removed through change control.
Evidence: Rule review workpaper with reviewer, date, rules examined, and resulting change tickets
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Inbound and outbound CDE traffic is restricted to what is necessary and denied by default. CDE databases have no internet route. Egress is through an allow-listed proxy. NSCs sit between trusted and untrusted networks.
Evidence: Security group and route table exports; VPC Reachability Analyzer results; proxy allow list
Test Procedure Ref: TP-AUTO (test of one plus ITGC reliance; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Network diagrams and cardholder data-flow diagrams are kept current and reviewed as part of each scope confirmation.
Evidence: Dated diagrams with reviewer approval; scope confirmation memo reference
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Company laptops that can reach the CDE are managed, run EDR and a host firewall, and connect to the CDE only through Okta and AWS Systems Manager Session Manager. Personal devices cannot reach the CDE.
Evidence: MDM compliance report; device trust policy in Okta; Session Manager access configuration
Test Procedure Ref: TP-AUTO (test of one plus ITGC reliance; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: No wireless networks connect to the CDE. Authorized wireless access points are inventoried with justification, and the colocation site is tested for unauthorized wireless access points every three months.
Evidence: Wireless inventory; quarterly wireless scan results for the colocation cage
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Stored PAN is rendered unreadable. The legacy batch database uses column-level encryption (not disk-level alone), cloud databases store gateway tokens and truncated PAN for new transactions, with pre-2025 encrypted PAN retained only until the DAT-01 purge, and PAN displays are masked to no more than the BIN and last four digits. SAD is never stored after authorization.
Evidence: Database encryption configuration; schema showing token and truncated columns; masked screen samples; PAN discovery results
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: PAN in transit over public networks (browser to hosted payment page, Keystone to gateway) uses TLS 1.2 or higher with strong ciphers and valid certificates. Non-console administrative access is encrypted. An inventory of trusted keys and certificates is maintained.
Evidence: Load balancer TLS policy; external TLS scan results; certificate inventory export
Test Procedure Ref: TP-AUTO (test of one plus ITGC reliance; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Keys that protect stored account data are managed through AWS KMS and, for the legacy system, a documented key hierarchy: secure generation, distribution, storage, defined cryptoperiods with rotation, retirement, split knowledge and dual control for any manual cleartext key operation, and signed key custodian acknowledgments.
Evidence: Key management procedures; KMS key policies and rotation status; key custodian forms; key ceremony log
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: An inventory of cryptographic cipher suites and protocols in use (purpose and location) is maintained and reviewed at least every 12 months, with a documented plan to respond to changes in cryptographic strength.
Evidence: Cipher and protocol inventory; annual review record
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: The incident response plan defines roles, communications, containment by incident type, notification of payment brands, acquirers, and state agency customers as contracts require, legal reporting analysis, business recovery, backups, and the procedure for PAN found where it is not expected. It is reviewed at least every 12 months and updated from lessons learned.
Evidence: IR plan with version history and approval; contact lists; lessons-learned updates
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: The incident response plan is tested at least every 12 months through a tabletop exercise (for example payment page skimming), with results and follow-up actions documented. The same exercise satisfies the GovRAMP annual IRP test.
Evidence: Tabletop agenda, attendance, scenario, after-action report, and tracked actions
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Designated incident responders are on call 24/7 and trained at the frequency set in the TRA.
Evidence: On-call schedule export; training records; TRA for training frequency
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Security incidents are logged in ServiceNow, classified by severity, tracked to closure with root cause, and summarized monthly to management.
Evidence: Incident register export; sampled incident tickets; monthly summary
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: A list of third-party service providers that handle or could affect account data is maintained with the services they provide, along with a responsibility matrix showing which PCI DSS requirements each TPSP manages, which Keystone manages, and which are shared.
Evidence: TPSP inventory; PCI responsibility matrix per TPSP
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: New vendors are risk tiered and go through security due diligence before contract. Contracts for vendors that handle or affect account data include written acknowledgment of their responsibility for account data security, breach notification, and right to audit or report provision.
Evidence: Due diligence file; tiering questionnaire; executed contract clauses
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: At least once every 12 months Keystone obtains and reviews each Tier 1 vendor's AOC and SOC reports: opinion, period and coverage gaps, bridge letter, exceptions, subservice organizations, and CUECs mapped to Keystone controls. Issues are logged in GOV-07.
Evidence: Completed SOC report review checklists; AOC copies; CUEC mapping; follow-up tickets
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Keystone gives state agency customers written acknowledgment of its responsibility for the account data it handles, and on request provides its AOC and a responsibility matrix of PCI DSS requirements it manages for them.
Evidence: Customer contract template clauses; customer responsibility matrix; log of AOC requests fulfilled
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Access to the Keystone cage at the colocation site requires badge and biometric authentication. The access list is reviewed quarterly. Entry to the cage is covered by video retained at least three months. Visitors are authorized, escorted, and logged.
Evidence: Colocation access list with quarterly review sign-off; video retention setting; visitor logs
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Media with cardholder data (legacy backup media) is classified, physically secured, inventoried at least every 12 months, and destroyed with a certificate of destruction when no longer needed.
Evidence: Media inventory with annual reconciliation; offsite storage records; destruction certificates
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Candidates who will have access to the CDE are background screened before hire, within the limits of local law.
Evidence: Background check completion report reconciled to new hire list
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: All personnel complete security awareness training on hire and every 12 months, including phishing, social engineering, and acceptable use of end-user technology, and acknowledge the security policy each year. The program is reviewed every 12 months.
Evidence: LMS completion report reconciled to HR roster; course content outline; acknowledgment records; program review record
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Automated anti-phishing controls protect personnel: DMARC at enforcement, inbound link rewriting and time-of-click checks, attachment sandboxing, and a report-phish button. Phishing simulations run quarterly.
Evidence: DNS DMARC record; email security configuration; simulation results
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Account data retention is limited by policy with a business justification per data type. At least every three months, a documented process confirms that stored account data past its retention period has been securely deleted.
Evidence: Retention schedule; quarterly purge job output and verification sign-off
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Quarterly automated PAN discovery (Amazon Macie for S3, DLP scans for file shares, logs, and ServiceNow attachments) looks for PAN outside the defined CDE. Any hit triggers the IR-01 procedure for PAN found where it is not expected.
Evidence: Discovery job configuration and results; tickets for hits with disposition
Test Procedure Ref: TP-STD (inspection of design and one or more instances; see 02-control-matrix/README.md)

Control Statement: Confidential agency data, including ACH bank account numbers and citizen PII, is classified and protected per the data classification standard and securely disposed of at contract end.
